seal.statement: A fresh CREATE whose replica has been admitted into its partition's committed configuration never turns an unavailable authority read into an orphaned configured member. The create-admission authorization of releaseFreshCreate answers a typed UNAVAILABLE{create_admission_authority, retryAfterMs, cause} that the existing participant-release completion operation consumes within the create's existing deadline, so a transient refusal of the replica_operations read (as at 10:29:57 on run b26d2c090) delays the create instead of failing it. When the create does fail after admission committed, its FAILED transition always carries the failed-create cleanup claim, so the existing failed-create cleanup owner removes the member through a committed REMOVE; the cleanup decision is made from the committed admission fact, never from error.deferRetry, and a FAILED row from a create in flight is protected from the planner's FAILED cure only while a claim or a live create owner exists. The one-shot authorization throw, the deferRetry-based claimCleanup arm and the unconditional previous_state protection are deleted.

U-f caller census (recorded before any deletion). claimCleanup:false on deferRetry exists for the coordinator's executor-outcome DEFER_RETRY state (critical system partition + retryable control-plane error + dispatch-retryable step PENDING/SENDING, or CREATING via isCreateRearmDispatchPhase): the same create identity is re-dispatched, so no cleanup claim may block it. Once the workflow is SYNCING the coordinator FAILs the operation (status reconcile or FAIL_OPERATION), so a deferRetry failure after the runtime opened is never re-armed and its missing claim orphans a configured member (r4). Planner: three arms protect a FAILED create target from the plain FAILED cure: (1) cleanup token claimed, (2) previous_state in PENDING/CREATING/SYNCING, (3) terminal FAILED create operation with no recorded claims (historicalFailedCreateClaimProtects returns true for empty claims). A claimed target is removed through decideFailedCreateTargetCleanup -> REMOVE with the lifecycle precondition (the path that removed r5, r6). Consequence: arm (2) is NOT what orphaned r4 - arm (3) alone protects r4 (its ADD c44b07a7 is terminal FAILED with no claim); the target-side claim is sufficient to make r4 removable. Arm (2) is redundant with hasPendingMove for an in-flight create only when the planner's cache shows the in-flight operation (census U10: cache-sourced); for a re-armed create whose operation row lags in the cache, arm (2) is the only protection against REMOVE racing the recreate. Deleting arm (2) is therefore not needed for B's invariant and removes a protection; reported to the lead for decision before deleting.

R17 finding for Group A attempt 3 (serve-eligibility-committed-epoch-read, C11 one operation source): the planner's FAILED-cure protection by previous_state (check 2, FAILED_CREATE_SOURCE_STATES) is itself an instance of the class: a carve-out compensating for the planner's cached view of in-flight operations (hasPendingMove reads getInFlightOperations from the cache). Check 2 becomes deletable once the planner reads the in-flight operation set from the authoritative source; until then it protects the re-dispatch race (a DEFER_RETRY re-dispatched create whose in-flight operation row lags in the planner cache).
